title: Norm-one retraction onto a finite ell-adic subfield
statement: Fix a prime $\ell$, an algebraic closure $\Omega/\mathbf Q_\ell$ with the extending nonarchimedean absolute value and its norm topology [def-weil-algebraic-closure], [def-weil-l-adic-numbers], and a finite intermediate extension $\mathbf Q_\ell\subseteq F\subseteq\Omega$ [def-weil-l-adic-coefficient-extension]. There exists an $F$-linear map $p_F:\Omega\to F$ with $p_F(a)=a$ for $a\in F$ and $|p_F(x)|\leq |x|$ for every $x\in\Omega$. In particular it is continuous. No completeness of $\Omega$ is assumed.

source.place: Paragraph (3), scalar tame-kernel expansion: uniformly bounded finite-field projections for a pointwise finite coefficient decomposition; agent-formulated auxiliary lemma, exact literature reference WANTED.

proof.text: Give $F$ the restriction of the specified absolute value on $\Omega$. It extends the $\ell$-adic absolute value, and $F/\mathbf Q_\ell$ is finite-dimensional by hypothesis, so by the uniqueness in [lem-weil-l-adic-extension-absolute-value] it is the extending absolute value $|\cdot|_F$ of $F$. Apply [lem-weil-l-adic-extension-proper] with $E=F$: every closed ball $\{b\in F:|b-a|\leq r\}$, $r\geq0$, is compact. We regard $\Omega$ as an $F$-vector space with norm $\|x\|=|x|$. Multiplicativity gives $\|ax\|=|a|\|x\|$, and its given nonarchimedean inequality gives $\|x+y\|\leq\max(\|x\|,\|y\|)$. The identity on the subspace $F\subseteq\Omega$ satisfies the bound $|a|\leq\|a\|$.

source.place: Paragraph (3), agent expansion of the norm-one finite-field projection input

proof.text:
For any $F$-subspace $U\subseteq\Omega$ containing $F$, any $F$-linear $g:U\to F$ restricting to the identity on $F$ with $|g(u)|\leq\|u\|$, and any $x\in\Omega\setminus U$, put $R_u=\|x-u\|$ and $B_u=\{b\in F:|b-g(u)|\leq R_u\}$ for $u\in U$. Linearity and the bound imply
$$|g(u)-g(v)|\leq\|u-v\|\leq\max(R_u,R_v).$$
If $R_u\leq R_v$ and $b\in B_u$, then $|b-g(v)|\leq\max(|b-g(u)|,|g(u)-g(v)|)\leq R_v$; hence $B_u\subseteq B_v$. Each ball contains its center. It is closed: if $y\notin B_u$, take $\epsilon=(|y-g(u)|-R_u)/2>0$; $|z-y|<\epsilon$ and $z\in B_u$ would give $|y-g(u)|\leq|y-z|+R_u<\epsilon+R_u<|y-g(u)|$. The ordinary triangle inequality used here follows from $\max(r,s)\leq r+s$ for nonnegative $r,s$.

source.place: Paragraph (3), agent expansion of the norm-one finite-field projection input

proof.text: The ball $B_0=\{b\in F:|b|\leq\|x\|\}$ is compact by step 1 and contains zero. For every finite subset $A\subseteq U$, select $u_*$ of least radius among $A\cup\{0\}$. The containment calculation of step 2 shows that $g(u_*)$ belongs to $B_0\cap\bigcap_{u\in A}B_u$. This also proves nonemptiness when $A=\varnothing$. Thus the closed subsets $B_0\cap B_u$ of the compact topological space $B_0$ have the finite intersection property. Apply [lem-sfb-compact-closed-finite-intersection] with index set $U$ to obtain $b\in F$ satisfying $|b-g(u)|\leq\|x-u\|$ for every $u\in U$. All compactness is in $F$; no compactness or completeness of $\Omega$ or $U$ is used.

source.place: Paragraph (3), agent projection expansion: compact finite intersection argument; Stacks Tag 005D, lemma-intersection-closed-in-quasi-compact

proof.text:
Every element of $U+Fx$ has a unique expression $u+ax$ with $u\in U$ and $a\in F$: a difference of two expressions with distinct coefficients would imply $x\in U$. Define $G(u+ax)=g(u)+ab$. Adding and scaling the unique expressions proves $F$-linearity; at $a=0$ the formula equals $g(u)$, so $G$ extends $g$ and fixes $F$. If $a\ne0$, let $v=-a^{-1}u\in U$. The inequality for $b$ yields
$$|G(u+ax)|=|a|\,|b-g(v)|\leq |a|\|x-v\|=\|u+ax\|.$$
For $a=0$ use the original bound on $g$. Thus $G$ is a contractive extension to a strictly larger subspace. The sign identities used here follow from $|-1|=1$, since $|-1|^2=1$. Steps 2–4 establish this extension construction for every such $U,g,x$.

source.place: Paragraph (3), agent expansion of the norm-one finite-field projection input

proof.text: Let $\mathcal S$ be the set of graphs in $\Omega\times F$ of all $F$-linear maps $g:U\to F$ with $F\subseteq U\subseteq\Omega$, $g|_F=\mathrm{id}_F$, and $|g(u)|\leq\|u\|$. This is a set of subsets of $\Omega\times F$, and the identity graph on $F$ belongs to it. For a nonempty inclusion-chain of these graphs take the union. Comparability makes the union single-valued; its domain is the union of the subspaces. Any two domain vectors belong together to one chain member, which verifies closure under addition and the linear identity there; scalar multiplication is verified in the member containing the vector. Thus the union is again a linear graph. It contains $F$, fixes $F$, and satisfies the same pointwise bound, each value being a value in a chain member. Hence it is an upper bound in $\mathcal S$. For the empty chain use the identity graph on $F$.

source.place: Paragraph (3), agent expansion of the norm-one finite-field projection input

proof.text: Apply [lem-weil-pbc-zorn-lemma] to $X=\Omega\times F$ and the set $\mathcal S$, using the upper bounds of step 5, including the empty chain. Obtain a maximal graph, of a map $g:U\to F$. If $U\ne\Omega$, choose $x\in\Omega\setminus U$. Steps 2–4, with this $U,g,x$, construct a contractive linear map $G:U+Fx\to F$ fixing $F$. Its graph belongs to $\mathcal S$ and strictly contains the graph of $g$, since it also contains a pair with first coordinate $x$. This contradicts maximality. Therefore $U=\Omega$, and set $p_F=g$.

source.place: Paragraph (3), agent expansion of the norm-one finite-field projection input

proof.text:
The defining conditions of $\mathcal S$ give $F$-linearity, $p_F(a)=a$ for every $a\in F$, and $|p_F(x)|\leq|x|$ for every $x\in\Omega$. For $x,y\in\Omega$,
$$|p_F(x)-p_F(y)|=|p_F(x-y)|\leq|x-y|.$$
Given $\epsilon>0$, choose $\delta=\epsilon$ in this inequality to obtain continuity for the specified norm topologies. At $x=1$ equality holds in the bound, so the map indeed has norm one. The argument never completes $\Omega$.
